__comment: ADR-0039 gives the Engineer's Pick the wrench's DISMANTLE verb, and this tag is what delivers it: dismantle rides the ordinary block-break path, which the Pick already answers with isCorrectToolForDrops, and GregTech resolves what counts as a wrench from tool tags. Confirmed in-game -- a machine breaks and drops its item. The tag does NOT carry the other verbs, and it looks as though it should: rotate and the configure verbs are gated on NeoForge ItemAbility declarations (GTItemAbilities.WRENCH_ROTATE, WRENCH_CONFIGURE and friends) that a plain Item answers false to. #168 settled which of those the Pick claims, in the jar rather than here -- PickAbilities grants wrench_rotate and the wrench_configure* abilities, which set a machine's auto-output face, and declines wrench_connect, the pipe-connection verb ADR-0017 leaves pointing at pipes Terra does not ship. Note the overlay this tag alone still drives: GTCEu draws the rotation highlight on `toolTypes.contains(WRENCH) || canPerformAction(WRENCH_ROTATE)`, an OR whose first half is this tag, so before #168 the highlight appeared while right-click did nothing. Removing this tag would therefore silence the overlay as well as the dismantle verb. This is GregTech's own, the tag `GTToolType.WRENCH` is built with. GTCEu reads both it and the NeoForge one next to this file; naming both is cheaper than depending on which check a given machine runs.
